hero.heading: Understanding inherited genetic disorders, together
hero.mission: Shared Blood helps families, caregivers, and communities across Pakistan understand inherited genetic disorders through clear, compassionate, evidence-based education.

intro.title: About Shared Blood
intro.paragraph: Inherited genetic disorders affect thousands of families in Pakistan. Shared Blood is an independent educational initiative that explains the science of inheritance in plain language, raises public awareness, and connects caregivers with community resources, so that every family can recognise early signs and make informed decisions with confidence.
objectives: Explain genetics in simple, accessible language.
intro.disclaimer: Shared Blood is an educational resource only. It does not provide medical diagnosis or advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional.

disclaimer.title: An educational tool, not a diagnosis
disclaimer.body: This calculator demonstrates simplified inheritance only when the inheritance pattern and both parents' relevant genetic statuses are known. It does not diagnose a condition, determine carrier status, interpret genetic test results, or calculate anyone's complete genetic risk. Discuss genetic test results and family-specific risk with a qualified healthcare professional or genetic counsellor.

disease.help: The condition determines which inheritance model applies. Some conditions depend on the specific subtype.

subtype.help: This condition's inheritance depends on the subtype, so a subtype must be chosen.

carrier.label: Carrier
carrier.definition: One altered, one typical copy (Aa). Usually no symptoms.

tested-negative.label: Tested negative
tested-negative.definition: No disease-causing variant detected by this model (AA).

affected.label: Affected
affected.definition: One variant copy (Aa). Modelled as affected under dominant inheritance.

errors.condition-missing: Please select a disorder or supported subtype before calculating inheritance.
errors.subtype-required: Please select a supported subtype before calculating inheritance.
errors.parent-one-missing: Please select the required genetic status of parent one.
errors.parent-two-missing: Please select the required genetic status of parent two.
errors.combination-unsupported: This parental combination requires condition-specific inheritance information and is not supported by the current simplified model.

unsupported.heading: This condition can't be modelled here

unknown.title: Not sure of a parent's genetic status?
unknown.body: This calculator needs the known genetic status of both parents. It cannot estimate carrier or affected status, or infer a genotype from relationship or population data. These pages can help:

results.heading: Results for each pregnancy
results.summary: Based on parent one ({one}) and parent two ({two}).
results.perPregnancyTitle: These chances apply to each pregnancy
results.perPregnancyBody: Each pregnancy is a separate, independent inheritance event with the same modelled chance. A percentage does not mean that exact fraction of a family's children will be affected.

affected.label: Affected
affected.explanation: A child who inherits two altered copies (one from each parent) and is modelled as affected by the condition.

carrier.label: Carrier
carrier.explanation: A child who inherits one altered and one typical copy. Carriers usually have no symptoms but can pass the altered copy on.

unaffected.label: Unaffected
unaffected.explanation: A child who inherits two typical copies, neither affected nor carrying the altered copy represented by this model.

inherits-variant.label: Inherits the variant
inherits-variant.explanation: A child who inherits the dominant variant and is modelled as affected under this simplified dominant model.

not-inherited.label: Does not inherit
not-inherited.explanation: A child who does not inherit the dominant variant and is modelled as unaffected.

viz.heading: Inheritance combinations
viz.caption: Each parent passes on one allele. These are the four equally likely combinations for a child:

disclaimer.title: An educational explorer, not a risk calculator
disclaimer.body: This tool explains why shared ancestry can raise the chance that both parents carry the same recessive variant. It does not calculate an individual couple's risk of a specific disease, infer anyone's genetic status, or provide a diagnosis. It uses neutral, educational language and makes no judgment about marriage.

relationship.help: Choose a biological relationship category to explore its genetics. This tool makes no social, religious, or legal judgment about marriage.

RelationshipExplorer.emptyState: Select a biological relationship above to see its Relationship Genetics Profile.

sections.recessiveSharing: How recessive variants can be shared

coefficient.meaning: The inbreeding coefficient (F) estimates the probability that, at a given point in the genome, a child inherits two copies of an allele that came from the same shared ancestor. It is not the chance of having a genetic disorder.
coefficient.complexLimit: This value represents the expected coefficient for the selected simple relationship pattern. A real family pedigree (with repeated cousin marriages or several shared ancestors) may produce a different value.
coefficient.unrelatedBody: This selection represents no known recent shared ancestry, so a simple-pedigree coefficient is not shown. Distant or population-level relatedness may still exist, and everyone carries some recessive variants.

pedigree.hypotheticalNote: This is an educational example. It does not mean the ancestor actually carried a disease-causing variant.

evidence.notConfigured: A single population-level risk estimate is not provided for this relationship category.

disease.help: This changes the educational explanation only. It does not change the coefficient or produce a disease-specific probability.

cannotTell.body: Relationship category alone cannot tell you whether two people carry the same disease-causing variant. More specific context depends on family history, known familial disease, carrier status, genetic testing, the specific disease or gene, and complex pedigrees.

knownStatus.label: Known parent genetic status
knownStatus.detail: Simplified Mendelian probabilities in the Inheritance Probability Calculator.

scenario.notGenotypeTitle: Relationship alone does not tell us genotype
scenario.notGenotypeBody: Being related does not tell us whether two people carry the same variant. The scenarios below are explicit, hypothetical examples; they are not based on your relationship, and they never estimate a real couple's risk.
scenario.intro: To understand how inheritance works, choose a hypothetical scenario and view its Punnett square.

notCompatibility.title: This is education, not a compatibility test
notCompatibility.body: Shared Blood helps you understand testing, carrier status, and counselling so you can make your own informed decisions. It never approves or rejects couples, never says anyone is “genetically compatible” or “incompatible”, and never tells anyone whether to marry or have children. Consanguineous marriage has real cultural and social significance; genetics education is about information, not judgement.

library.title: Testing education topics
library.intro: Browse curated topics, or narrow them by context, audience, category, or condition. Choosing a context only filters the education shown; it never works out your personal risk.

screening.title: Screening vs diagnostic testing
screening.intro: These are different kinds of test with different purposes. The exact meaning varies by test.
screening.screeningBody: Screening estimates whether there may be an increased chance of a condition. A screening result is not a diagnosis.
screening.diagnosticBody: Diagnostic testing is used to determine whether a specific condition or finding is present, often after screening or when there is a clinical reason.
screening.note: Which test is right, and what a result means, is explained by a healthcare professional in each person's context.

results.disclaimer: Meaning depends on the test, the genes and variants, the condition, the clinical context, and current knowledge. Only a qualified professional can explain a specific result.

ethics.title: Privacy, respect, and your decisions
ethics.privacyBody: Genetic information can be sensitive and may have implications for biological relatives. It is worth asking any provider how your information is stored, used, and shared. Shared Blood does not collect genetic results.
ethics.stigmaBody: A family with a known history of an inherited condition is exactly that, not a “risky” or “bad” family. Carriers and affected people deserve respect, free of stigma toward any community, caste, or biradari.
ethics.bothParentsBody: Children inherit genetic information from both biological parents. In autosomal recessive conditions, a child may inherit one disease-associated variant from each parent; this is never one parent's, or one mother's, fault.
ethics.ethicsBody: Religious beliefs, family values, and personal ethics are yours. You may discuss these questions with qualified healthcare professionals and trusted advisors. Shared Blood does not give religious rulings or make personal decisions for you.

overview.title: About this research
overview.purpose: Shared Blood studies what people know, do not know, and believe about inherited conditions, carrier status, family history, and genetic testing, and how awareness relates to family and social context. It reports aggregate findings from people who chose to take part in a survey.
overview.disclaimer: These findings describe the people who participated in the survey. They may show patterns within the survey sample, but should not automatically be read as representing all people in Pakistan or all residents of the surveyed cities.

Community.title: Shared Blood in the Community
Community.subtitle: Taking genetic health education beyond the screen.

intro.title: Our community work
intro.body: Shared Blood applies its scientific and educational work outside the website through direct community engagement: childcare-worker education, awareness sessions, and learning-booklet distribution. This page documents what we did, who it was for, what we delivered, what we measured, what we observed, and how that work changed the project.
intro.positioning: We frame community work as educational collaboration and public-health awareness, not saving communities from their traditions. We prioritise evidence of work over promotional language, and we recognise the family structures, healthcare access, and existing knowledge of the people we work with.

impact.title: Documented impact
impact.subtitle: Every total below is derived from approved, completed activity records, not typed by hand.

metrics.recordedNote: Recorded attendance, not unique people; some may have attended more than once.
metrics.bookletNote: A booklet distributed is a resource, not a person educated.

focus.title: Current fieldwork focus
focus.body: Our initial fieldwork spans these activity types. The architecture is not built only around orphanages and can grow to new audiences and regions.

childcare.title: Childcare-worker education
childcare.body: We help childcare workers caring for infants and young children learn about inherited conditions, symptoms that may appear in infancy, and supportive growth considerations.
childcare.boundary: Childcare workers learn to recognise possible warning signs and seek appropriate medical evaluation, not to diagnose or confirm a disorder.

booklet.title: Learning booklets
booklet.body: Our learning booklets are versioned educational resources. Each fieldwork record references the exact resource version used, and distributed booklets are counted separately from people educated.

learnings.title: What we learned in the field

changed.narrative: We researched, we built, we took it into the community, we listened, and we changed the project.

activity.observationNote: These observations are contextual to this activity and are not claims about any city or population.

methodology.title: Fieldwork methodology & limitations
methodology.pending: Full methodology will be published alongside the first approved activities.
methodology.limitRepeat: Some participants may have attended more than one activity (repeat attendance).
methodology.limitEstimated: Estimated attendance is approximate, not a verified count.
methodology.limitBooklets: A booklet distributed does not equal a person educated.
methodology.limitRetention: Immediate knowledge change does not equal long-term retention.
methodology.limitObservations: Field observations are contextual, not epidemiological samples, and fieldwork locations are not disease epicentres.
methodology.disclaimer: This page documents Shared Blood's community activities and aggregate impact. It does not create profiles of participants, children, or patients, and it does not estimate hypothetical lives saved or diseases prevented.

empty.title: Community work is being documented
empty.body: Shared Blood's community work is currently being documented for publication. Approved activities and aggregate impact will appear here once they have been reviewed. Planned activities are never shown as completed impact.

Research.title: Research & Findings
Research.subtitle: What Shared Blood is learning through research and community work.

intro.title: How we do research
intro.body: Shared Blood turns approved survey findings and documented community work into structured, reviewed research outputs. Each finding shows what was studied, where the evidence came from, what evidence type supports it, how it was calculated, what it does and does not show, and how it changed the project.
intro.disclaimer: These findings describe the datasets, survey samples, and documented activities they were produced from, and should be read within their methodology and limitations. Shared Blood research is educational and public-health focused and does not provide individual medical diagnosis.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.representativeNote: Sample size and representativeness are separate. A convenience sample is not representative of Pakistan, and national scope is used only where the evidence supports it.

Policy.title: Policy & Advocacy
Policy.subtitle: Turning genetic-health evidence into practical educational priorities.

intro.title: Our educational advocacy
intro.body: Shared Blood turns approved research findings and documented fieldwork into clearly-bounded advocacy priorities for genetic-health education. Every priority explains the issue, the evidence, the recommended educational response, who could act, and, crucially, what the advocacy does not claim.
intro.disclaimer: Shared Blood's advocacy focuses on genetic-health education, awareness, and public-health communication. Recommendations are based on the evidence and limitations identified in each priority and do not represent government policy or individual medical advice. Shared Blood is not a government authority.

scopeSection.title: What Shared Blood advocates for
scopeSection.body: Version 1 advocacy stays aligned with Shared Blood's educational mission and remains voluntary, non-coercive, and non-stigmatizing.

evidenceBehind.title: Evidence behind our advocacy
evidenceBehind.intro: Each advocacy priority is supported by one or more evidence types. Each type keeps its research interpretation boundary.
evidenceBehind.RESEARCH_FINDING: Reviewed Shared Blood research findings, bounded by their sample and limitations.
evidenceBehind.SURVEY_FINDING: Approved survey findings describing the surveyed sample, not the population.
evidenceBehind.FIELDWORK_METRIC: Documented Shared Blood activity records, not general-population measures.
evidenceBehind.FIELD_OBSERVATION: Contextual observations from documented sessions, not national knowledge levels.
evidenceBehind.TRAINING_ASSESSMENT: Aggregate assessment results measuring immediate change only.
evidenceBehind.LITERATURE_SOURCE: External published research, attributed to its source.
evidenceBehind.PROJECT_OPERATIONAL_DATA: Approved project execution data describing Shared Blood's own work.

intro.title: About the Punnett Square
intro.body: A Punnett square is a simple grid that shows how the alleles two parents could pass on combine. It visualises the probabilities from the Inheritance Probability Calculator; it does not calculate anything on its own.

calculator.body: Pick a condition and parent statuses to see the probabilities and the matching Punnett square.

About.title: About Shared Blood
About.intro: Shared Blood is an educational platform about inherited genetic disorders in Pakistan. It helps families, students, and communities understand genetics in clear, respectful language.

mission.heading: Our mission
mission.body: Understanding Genetics. Supporting Families. Building Healthier Futures. We aim to make trustworthy, plain-language education about inherited conditions freely available in English and Urdu.

approach.heading: Our approach
approach.body: Every topic is explained in plain language, in both English and Urdu, and is grounded in established science. We focus on understanding and support, never judgement of families, communities, or personal decisions.

notWhat.heading: What Shared Blood is not
notWhat.body: Shared Blood is an educational resource. It is not a hospital, clinic, laboratory, or diagnostic service, and it does not provide medical diagnosis, testing, or personal risk assessment.

disclaimer.heading: Not medical advice
disclaimer.body: Shared Blood is an educational resource and does not provide medical diagnosis or advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional or genetic counselor.
